title: Cohere API Trial Key, Rate Limits and Pricing in 2026
summary: The Cohere API enables developers to integrate advanced retrieval-augmented generation and tool-calling features into production-grade applications.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Does Cohere use my API data for training?


Cohere does not use data submitted through their production API to train their base models. This separation ensures that proprietary prompt engineering and sensitive customer inputs remain isolated from the global weights of the Command model family.


While many consumer-facing chatbots utilize user interactions for reinforcement learning, Cohere’s enterprise-facing API treats data as transient for the purpose of inference.


Even if Cohere itself has discarded the data, your information is subject to the intermediary’s retention policy when you access these models through a third-party reseller. The platform provider might store your logs in a plain-text database.


### How do I increase my rate limits for production?


Transitioning from the trial tier to a production organization and providing a valid payment method is required to increase rate limits.


You must use production keys for live traffic because trial keys will trigger HTTP 429 errors if you attempt to run high-volume concurrent loops. To move beyond these initial constraints, you must request a quota increase through the dashboard.


If you are building agentic workflows using high-reasoning models like Claude Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra alongside Cohere for embeddings, you must manage these limits independently for each provider.


High-volume systems often require a centralized rate-limiting proxy to queue requests. This prevents a single runaway loop from exhausting your entire monthly budget in minutes.


### Can I self-host Cohere models via VPC?


By utilizing managed cloud environments like Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI, you can deploy Cohere models within a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).


A VPC is a private, isolated section of a public cloud provider’s network that allows you to run resources in a virtual network you define. This deployment strategy ensures that data never traverses the public internet, satisfying strict compliance requirements for financial or medical data.


When using these managed services, you retain the ability to toggle safety filters and manage model versions directly. This is often restricted when using a standard API wrapper.


Amazon Bedrock is an AWS service that is an access point for foundation models via an API without managing underlying infrastructure. Google Cloud Vertex AI is a machine learning platform that allows you to train and deploy AI models and applications.


Azure AI Studio is a platform for developing and deploying generative AI applications within the Microsoft ecosystem.


Each of these environments allows you to provision "Provisioned Throughput," which guarantees a specific level of performance for your application.


This is the preferred path for senior engineers who need to ensure that a critical production agent has dedicated compute resources that cannot be throttled by other users on a shared multi-tenant API.
